$comment: Real device geometry, in LOGICAL units — points on iOS, dp on Android, CSS
pixels in a browser. These are the numbers layout actually sees; physical
pixel counts and screen diagonals are not.
This file is the single source of truth for the device matrix. Both the
Flutter layout system (apps/mobile/lib/src/layout.dart) and the verifier
(verify.mjs) are checked against it, and the verifier fails if they drift.
The point of the table is NOT to special-case devices. It is to establish
the RANGE the layout has to survive, and to give the verifier real widths
to run the rules at. No code should ever branch on a device name.
Material 3 window size classes, unchanged. Guardrail G10 says convention
wins where familiarity lowers error rates, and inventing a parallel set of
breakpoints next to the ones the widget library already uses is exactly
the sort of gratuitous difference that costs more than it earns.
narrow is ours, and it sits INSIDE compact: 344dp (Galaxy Z Fold outer
screen) is 60dp tighter than a 404dp iPhone, and that gap is the
difference between a composer with room for a label and one without.
